How did the 2013 stage builder turn a page into islands?
items.answer: PhantomJS took a screenshot and the div/img boxes; a C++ stage_builder (OpenCV, Boost) removed the most common (background) colour, dilated, blurred and thresholded text into solid blobs (islands), bridged each island to its nearest neighbours, carved a maze with a randomized depth-first search, and placed start, goal, items and rails before returning JSON.

items.question: What did AI agents do in this rebuild?
items.answer: Claude Code agents (Claude Opus 5.5) wrote the code, tests and build logs, orchestrated by a main Claude Code session, with the owner directing and approving. At runtime the only model call is the docent. AI stage theming, naming, music and moderation were planned but not built.

items.question: Who made the original World Wide Maze?
items.answer: Google Japan with the Tokyo agency PARTY; AID-DCC, Katamari and FUTUREK (backend) are credited; Saqoosha wrote the engineering case study. Not a complete list of individuals.

items.question: Does the game use AI to theme stages?
items.answer: No. AI semantic theming was proposed in the research plan and the optional AI Remix phase, but it was never built; the stage builder is deterministic code.

items.question: Is there an AI Remix mode?
items.answer: No. AI Remix (Phase 11) was optional and never started.

items.question: Does AI moderate captured pages?
items.answer: No. The moderation hook lets all content through; abuse is handled with rate limits, a kill switch, takedown/opt-out and a word-list filter for leaderboard names.

items.question: Does an AI model write the stage names or choose the music?
items.answer: No. That was an idea in the research plan; the music is a fixed set of synthesized loops and no model names stages.

items.question: Which AI model runs in the live site, and for what?
items.answer: Only the docent: Claude (claude-haiku-4-5 by default) through Cloudflare AI Gateway, answering from the project's own sources with citations.

items.question: In 2013, how did the original builder merge lines of text into solid shapes?
items.answer: It removed the most common colour, then applied dilate, Gaussian blur and threshold (OpenCV) so fine text merged into solid blobs; image rectangles were filled solid.

items.question: Where did Saqoosha's stage builder place the start and the goal?
items.answer: At points farthest from the island edges (distance transform): the top-left one became the start, the bottom-right one the goal, and up to six others held large items.
